title: Pentametallic lanthanide-alkoxide square-based pyramids: high energy barrier for thermal relaxation in a holmium single molecule magnet

synthesis.procedure: React freshly generated potassium isopropoxide with anhydrous SmCl3 in isopropanol/toluene, adding a stoichiometric amount of water. The main article refers to the ESI for further preparation details but gives no numerical reagent quantity.

reagents.name: anhydrous SmCl3
reagents.amount: analogous-method reference quantity: 4.27 mmol; individual mass not stated

synthesis.time: Analogous method to 2: chloride added after 1 h; stirred for at least 48 h.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Standard Schlenk and glovebox techniques under dry nitrogen.
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Analogous method to 2: filter through dry Celite, remove volatile solvents in vacuo, dissolve solid in minimum n-hexane, filter, store overnight at −20 °C, then isolate crystals by filtration and dry in vacuo.

properties.summary: The susceptibility decreases on cooling, mainly attributed to single-ion crystal-field effects. Clear slow magnetization relaxation was not observed in the reported ac measurements.

source_locations.location: Experimental; synthesis of compound 2 and immediately following analogous-method statement for compounds 1, 3, 4 and 5

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: Five six-coordinate Sm sites form a square-based pyramid around a central μ5-oxide. Each metal bears a terminal isopropoxide; additional isopropoxides bridge triangular faces and basal edges. Compound 1 is reported as isostructural with 2.

properties.summary: Compound 4 shows clear frequency-dependent slow magnetization relaxation and is identified as a holmium single-molecule magnet. Applied dc fields enhance the high-temperature relaxation process. Above 24 K, Arrhenius analysis gives a thermal relaxation barrier of 400 ± 5 K; relaxation deviates from Arrhenius behavior at lower temperatures.

measurements.conditions: Ac susceptibility; 1.2 kHz; observed in zero dc field and at 3.5 and 5.5 kG dc fields

measurements.conditions: Cole–Cole analysis; 1.8 K; zero dc field

measurements.name: thermal relaxation barrier ΔE
measurements.conditions: Arrhenius fit above 24 K; dc fields of 3.5 and 5.5 kG

measurements.name: Arrhenius prefactor τ0
measurements.conditions: Arrhenius fit above 24 K; dc fields of 3.5 and 5.5 kG

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The crystal structure shown in Fig. 1 has five six-coordinate Ho sites at the vertices of a square-based pyramid surrounding a central μ5-oxide. Each site bears a terminal isopropoxide; four isopropoxides bridge triangular faces and four μ2-isopropoxides bridge basal edges. The article reports that 4 has the same unit cell as a previously reported polymorph of the Dy analogue 6 and a known polymorph of Er compound 5.
